name: Nizaa
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 5 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Theil Endresen, Rolf. 1992. La phonologie de la langue nizaa (nizaà). Nordic Journal of African Studies 1(1): 28-52. (open access,https://www.njas.fi/njas/article/view/57)
catalog_locator: sect. 5 'La tonologie', 5.1 'Les tons', p. 43; supporting: 5.2 'Le downstep' p. 46, 5.3 'La tonologie des substantifs polysyllabiques' p. 47, sect. 1.2 rule (1.3) 'Un substantif doit contenir au moins deux mores' p. 32
catalog_quote: 5 La tonologie 5.1 Les tons La tonologie du nizaa est relativement complexe. ... Le nizaa a un système tonologique à trois hauteurs distinctives: H(aut), M(oyen) et B(as). L'opposition entre M et B est subordonnée à celle entre H et non-H ... Mais le nizaa n'a pas seulement les trois tons H, M et B. En negligeant le downstep et les tons flottants, il nous faut distinguer neuf tons différents pour obtenir une description suffisante. Outre les trois tons simples, H, M et B, il s'agit de cinq tons doubles, HM, HB, MH, MB et BH, et un ton triple, BHM.

tone_statements.summary: Confirms lexical tone and adds the system the catalog rule leaves blank: three distinctive levels H, M, B with M/B subordinate to the H vs non-H split (tree (5.1), p. 43); monosyllabic verbs have a single lexical tone opposition, H vs non-H (p. 43); monosyllabic nouns carry ten lexical tones H°, HM, HB, M, M°, MB, B, B°, BH, BHM, where ° is a floating H (p. 44); floating H is deleted before pause

sources.citation: Theil Endresen, Rolf. 1992. La phonologie de la langue nizaa (nizaà). Nordic Journal of African Studies 1(1): 28-52.
sources.note: Full segmental + tonal phonology (sect. 1 syllable, 2 vowels, 3 consonants, 5 'La tonologie': three levels H/M/B, nine lexical tones incl. contours HM HB MH MB BH BHM, downstep, floating H, tone transport). No word for accent/stress/prominence anywhere in the publisher's scanned text (checked both layout and raw extracted text; scanned is garbled because the scan is 2-up, so a missed line is possible but unlikely).

sources.citation: Kjelsvik, Bjørghild. 2002. Verb chains in Nizaa. MA (cand.philol.) thesis, University of Oslo. 189 pp.
sources.note: Ch. 2.1 Phonology (pp. 9-13): syllable types CV/CVV/CVC, 5+10+7 vowels, 61 onset / 10 coda consonants, coda weakening, 2.1.5 Tones: 'three tone levels, high (H), mid (M) and low (L).. combined to complex tones', downstep, tone transport. Nothing on stress or accent.

sources.note: 4.4.1 Language description (pp. 111-113) and 4.4.2 Tones (pp. 112-114): 'a rich tonology, with three distinctive tonelevels and a number of tone combinations used as lexical tones.. tones are regularily transported', refers to Endresen 1992 for the full system. sources.note: Citing source only: Kjelsvik 2002 sect. 2.5, which she says is based on this MS, states that Nizaa verbs have two lexical tones (H vs M/non-high), that derivational suffixes have no inherent tone, and that tone marks verbal forms (imperative = a L tone attached to the verb root; subjunctive characterised by L tone) - i.e. the MS very likely describes grammatical tone in the verb paradigm; contents themselves unseen.
